section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section reviews the literature on associations between body image and sexual health outcomes, particularly in women. The authors discuss limitations in prior research, including the tendency to operationalize body image as the absence of negative body image rather than measuring positive body image directly, wide variation in operationalization of sexual liberalism, focus primarily on women rather than men, and reliance on small samples of college-aged individuals. The section establishes the rationale for examining associations between positive body image and sexual outcomes.
